records.title: OFAC designation press release — sanctions nexus, Nicosia Corporate Registry entity
records.text:
1. SOURCE. US Treasury OFAC press release. Subject: SDN list designation of ORYX POWER GROUP (Abu Dhabi) under Executive Order 13846 (Iran sanctions).

2. DESIGNATION BASIS. OFAC determined that the named entity provided material support to Iran's petroleum sector by purchasing Iranian crude oil and obscuring its origin through ship-to-ship transfers in international waters, with final documentation showing the cargo as originating from a non-sanctioned jurisdiction. The entity maintained a correspondent banking relationship with DESERT FALCON ENERGY (Dubai).

3. ANALYTICAL SIGNIFICANCE. The OFAC 50% rule (31 C.F.R. § 501.801) means that any entity ≥50% owned by the designated party is itself treated as sanctioned, regardless of whether it appears on the SDN list by name. Nexus to DESERT FALCON ENERGY (Dubai) via correspondent banking triggers KRI-02 (sanctions evasion nexus). This is directly analogous to the Vitol 2020 DPA in which Vitol processed crude oil of Iranian and Iraqi origin through intermediaries to obscure provenance. OFAC designation is a public record; reliability A, credibility 1 (confirmed).

records.title: TMS Alert — UNDISCLOSED_TRANSFER — TERRACINA MARITIME LTD (Nassau) SPV flow, Nicosia Corporate Registry
records.text:
1. SITUATION. Reconciliation of TERRACINA MARITIME LTD (Nassau)'s consolidated accounts against correspondent banking SWIFT data identified a transfer of $44.0M from NEH-Geneva to NKOSI TRADING & BROKERAGE (Lagos) (incorporated Nicosia Corporate Registry) on 28 Jun 2026 that does not appear in the consolidated financial statements for the corresponding period. The transfer carries SWIFT reference code MT202COV (cover payment), commonly used to obscure the originator of correspondent bank transfers.

2. 1MDB PARALLEL. The 1MDB scandal's core mechanism involved exactly this structure: Goldman Sachs bond proceeds were transferred from 1MDB to Good Star Limited (BVI, controlled by Jho Low) via MT202COV payments that bypassed standard beneficiary scrutiny. The FATF (2021) specifically identified MT202COV misuse as a high-risk AML typology. The present transfer's use of this code for an intra-group payment lacks commercial justification.

3. ASSESSMENT. The combination of off-balance-sheet treatment and MT202COV coding represents a KRI-01 (financial fraud/concealment) indicator at confidence level HIGH. Evaluation: A1 — PRIORITY. Legal hold on documentation required.

records.title: TMS Alert — REPORTING_GAP — PETROSERV ASIA PTE (Singapore), Cayman Islands
records.text:
1. SITUATION. The transaction monitoring system (TMS) recorded a REPORTING_GAP event for PETROSERV ASIA PTE (Singapore) on the Cayman Islands desk. Trade reporting to the relevant repository (DTCC / REGIS-TR) was suspended for 18 hours and 24 minutes from 09:56Z 28 Jun 2026. The gap spans a period during which independent market data shows five commodity trades were executed by PETROSERV ASIA PTE (Singapore)-registered counterparties in the OPIS Platts window.

2. PATTERN SIGNIFICANCE. The 18.4-hour gap is the primary reportable event. Review of the prior 90-day trade reporting history shows no comparable interruption, making this a departure from established behaviour rather than a system fault. 3. CROSS-REFERENCE. Five trades executed during the gap period involve counterparties also flagged in KRI-02 screening (sanctions nexus via NKOSI TRADING & BROKERAGE (Lagos)). TMS evaluation: A1 — PRIORITY.

records.title: Field report — Regulatory Liaison — Swiss FINMA correspondent — SPV structure, Geneva Trading Hub
records.text:
A. REPORT. Regulatory Liaison — Swiss FINMA correspondent describes a network of three SPVs incorporated in Geneva Trading Hub between Q3 2022 and Q1 2024, each with a single purpose: to hold a participation interest in a specific cargo trade executed by NEH Dubai Commodities DMCC. The source states that the SPV participations were never disclosed in NEXUS ENERGY HOLDINGS (Cayman)'s consolidated accounts, despite the parent company providing the credit support for all three. The source believes the SPVs were structured specifically to avoid consolidation under IFRS 10 (control-based consolidation standard).

B. SIGNIFICANCE. If the source's account is accurate, this is an off-balance-sheet structuring scheme of the type Enron used via its Raptor SPEs. Under IFRS 10, an entity controls an SPV if it has power over the investee, exposure to variable returns, and the ability to use that power — providing credit support almost certainly establishes all three. Non-consolidation in those circumstances would constitute a material misstatement.

C. COLLECTION NOTE. Location: Geneva Trading Hub. Duration: 43 minutes. Documentary evidence described but not yet provided. Source reliability: A. Credibility: 3 (possibly true pending documentation).

records.title: TMS Alert — FICTITIOUS_RECEIVABLE — NEXUS ENERGY HOLDINGS (Cayman) payment processor, Cayman Islands
records.text:
1. SITUATION. The internal audit function, cross-referencing accounts receivable against cash collection records, identified 16 receivable balances totalling $224.6M attributed to a Cayman Islands-registered payment processor ('PSP ALPHA CAY') that has no corporate registry entry, no website, and no independently verifiable business activity. The receivables have been carried for 326 days without cash collection.

2. WIRECARD PARALLEL. This is structurally identical to the Wirecard fraud: €1.9B was booked as escrow receivables from 'third-party acquirers' in Asia (primarily the Senjo Group), none of which had verifiable independent existence. KPMG's 2020 special audit could not verify the existence of the cash because it did not exist. The 180+ day non-collection on phantom receivables is precisely the pattern that should have triggered escalation in the Wirecard case.

3. ASSESSMENT. KRI-01 threshold met. Evaluation: A1 — FLASH. Recommend: (a) immediate write-down provisioning; (b) engagement of forensic accountants; (c) notification to auditors; (d) assessment of disclosure obligations under MAR Article 17.

records.text:
1. CONTENT. A Telegram channel focusing on offshore corporate structures published a corporate registry lookup showing five companies registered at the same Malta Financial Services address, all incorporated on the same date in 2023, with overlapping directors. One of the five — DESERT FALCON ENERGY (Dubai) — appears as a counterparty in a public court filing involving NEH Geneva Trading SA.

2. CHANNEL. The channel has operated for 847 days and has 4,219 subscribers. Two previous posts by this channel have been corroborated by subsequent regulatory filings. No platform verification. Automation indicator: LOW. Source grade: C.

3. ANALYTICAL NOTE. Same-address, same-date incorporation of multiple entities sharing directors is a corporate structuring red flag documented in the Panama Papers methodology guide (ICIJ, 2016) and in FATF's 2022 guidance on beneficial ownership opacity. This pattern alone does not establish criminality; it establishes that the structure warrants KYC escalation and beneficial ownership tracing under KRI-04.

records.title: Field report — External Informant — Nigerian anti-corruption agency liaison — PEP payment authorisation, Malta Financial Services
records.text:
A. REPORT. External Informant — Nigerian anti-corruption agency liaison states that a senior official (Sec. MBEKI Sipho (DRC Mining Cadastre Director)) was the undisclosed beneficial recipient of a consultancy contract awarded by NKOSI TRADING & BROKERAGE (Lagos) in 2023. The contract was nominally awarded to BEACON CAPITAL BROKERS (Nicosia), but the source witnessed the official personally directing the commercial terms and receiving reports that were not shared with the nominal consultant. The contract value was $12.7M annually.

B. PEP EXPOSURE SIGNIFICANCE. A PEP acting as undisclosed beneficial owner of a commercial contract with a company seeking government licences or contracts is a paradigm case of the corruption pattern documented in the Petrobras Lava Jato investigation. The Glencore Nigeria settlement (2022) involved a structurally identical arrangement with a petroleum ministry official (Jide Omokore) as undisclosed beneficial owner of intermediary companies.

C. COLLECTION NOTE. Duration: 55 minutes. Corroboration: PARTIAL — public tender records show the contract was awarded but no procurement competition is documented. Source grade: B. Credibility: 2.

records.title: TMS Alert — COMMODITY_MISMATCH — PETROSERV ASIA PTE (Singapore) cargo documentation, Abu Dhabi Global Market
records.text:
1. SITUATION. An automated cross-referencing of trade finance documents against commodity inspection certificates identified a COMMODITY_MISMATCH for a cargo associated with PETROSERV ASIA PTE (Singapore). The letter of credit issued by ABN AMRO describes the cargo as 'Iraqi Basrah Light crude, origin Iraq, 812Kt metric tonnes'. Independent inspection certification (SGS) describes the same cargo's sulphur content and API gravity as inconsistent with Basrah Light specifications and more consistent with Kharg Island (Iranian) crude.

2. PRECEDENT. This is the precise mechanism used in Vitol's 2020 DOJ/DPA: Iranian crude was shipped to Malaysia for STS transfer, re-documented as Malaysian condensate, then sold into international markets as non-sanctioned product. Vitol paid $135M under that agreement. The technical fingerprinting (sulphur content, density, trace metal profile) is the same detection method that identified Vitol's cargo.

3. ASSESSMENT. KRI-02 (sanctions evasion) and KRI-05 (commodity misreporting) thresholds met simultaneously. Evaluation: A1 — IMMEDIATE. Document hold and regulatory notification required.

records.title: Court filing — TERRACINA MARITIME LTD (Nassau) vs. TRIDENT ADVISORY GROUP (Dubai), Lugano Private Banking High Court
records.text:
1. SOURCE. Excerpt from a publicly available civil claim filed in Lugano Private Banking High Court. Plaintiff: TERRACINA MARITIME LTD (Nassau). Defendant: FAROUK ASSOCIATES LLC (Geneva).

2. RELEVANT PLEADING. Paragraph 34 of the particulars of claim alleges that the defendant received $14.7 million in 'advisory fees' between January 2023 and November 2025 in connection with 'facilitation services' in West Africa, and that no substantive advisory work was performed in exchange for those payments. The claimant characterises these payments as misappropriated funds routed through an intermediary structure.

3. ASSESSMENT. The payment description — large advisory fees to a third-party intermediary for 'facilitation services' with no deliverable — is the textbook structure identified in the Glencore DOJ consent order (2022), where $29.5M was paid to Dag Cramer via Wallbrook Ltd for Nigeria oil liftings. The claim does not assert criminality, but if the pleaded facts are proven, they would be consistent with KRI-03 (bribery/corruption via intermediary). The filing is a public record; reliability: A1.

records.title: TMS Alert — ROUND_TRIP_TRADE — PETROSERV ASIA PTE (Singapore) / CARACAS VENTURE ENERGIA (Venezuela), British Virgin Islands
records.text:
1. SITUATION. The trade surveillance platform identified a ROUND_TRIP_TRADE pattern involving PETROSERV ASIA PTE (Singapore) and counterparty VOYAGER PETROCHEMICALS LTD (Malta) on the British Virgin Islands desk. A crude oil cargo of $20.9M notional was sold on 29 Jun 2026 and repurchased 8 business days later at within 0.4% of the original price, with no apparent change in physical custody of the underlying commodity.

2. REGULATORY CONTEXT. Round-trip or wash trading in commodity markets violates Section 9(a)(2) of the Commodity Exchange Act (CFTC enforcement) and MiFID II Article 38 (MAR). Glencore's 2019–2022 price manipulation scheme used structurally similar round-trip trades to create artificial volume in fuel oil derivatives, settling a CFTC action for $341.2M in 2022. The present pattern matches that typology in form.

3. ASSESSMENT. Evaluation: B2 — IMMEDIATE. Two additional round-trip sequences detected in the prior 30-day window; this represents a pattern, not an isolated event. KRI-06 threshold met.

records.text:

3. ASSESSMENT. KRI-02 (sanctions evasion) and KRI-05 (commodity misreporting) thresholds met simultaneously. Evaluation: A1 — IMMEDIATE. Document hold and regulatory notification required.

records.text:

records.title: TMS Alert — COMMODITY_MISMATCH — ORYX POWER GROUP (Abu Dhabi) cargo documentation, Malta Financial Services
records.text:

records.title: Field report — External Informant — competitor trading house analyst — SPV structure, Lugano Private Banking
records.text:
A. REPORT. External Informant — competitor trading house analyst describes a network of three SPVs incorporated in Lugano Private Banking between Q3 2022 and Q1 2024, each with a single purpose: to hold a participation interest in a specific cargo trade executed by NEH Dubai Commodities DMCC. The source states that the SPV participations were never disclosed in NEXUS ENERGY HOLDINGS (Cayman)'s consolidated accounts, despite the parent company providing the credit support for all three. The source believes the SPVs were structured specifically to avoid consolidation under IFRS 10 (control-based consolidation standard).

B. SIGNIFICANCE. If the source's account is accurate, this is an off-balance-sheet structuring scheme of the type Enron used via its Raptor SPEs. Under IFRS 10, an entity controls an SPV if it has power over the investee, exposure to variable returns, and the ability to use that power — providing credit support almost certainly establishes all three. Non-consolidation in those circumstances would constitute a material misstatement.

C. COLLECTION NOTE. Location: Lugano Private Banking. Duration: 45 minutes. Documentary evidence described but not yet provided. Source reliability: C. Credibility: 3 (possibly true pending documentation).

records.title: TMS Alert — COMMODITY_MISMATCH — ORYX POWER GROUP (Abu Dhabi) cargo documentation, Dubai Free Zone
records.text:
1. SITUATION. An automated cross-referencing of trade finance documents against commodity inspection certificates identified a COMMODITY_MISMATCH for a cargo associated with ORYX POWER GROUP (Abu Dhabi). The letter of credit issued by Standard Chartered describes the cargo as 'Iraqi Basrah Light crude, origin Iraq, 1610Kt metric tonnes'. Independent inspection certification (SGS) describes the same cargo's sulphur content and API gravity as inconsistent with Basrah Light specifications and more consistent with Kharg Island (Iranian) crude.

2. PRECEDENT. This is the precise mechanism used in Vitol's 2020 DOJ/DPA: Iranian crude was shipped to Malaysia for STS transfer, re-documented as Malaysian condensate, then sold into international markets as non-sanctioned product. Vitol paid $135M under that agreement. The technical fingerprinting (sulphur content, density, trace metal profile) is the same detection method that identified Vitol's cargo.

3. ASSESSMENT. KRI-02 (sanctions evasion) and KRI-05 (commodity misreporting) thresholds met simultaneously. Evaluation: A1 — IMMEDIATE. Document hold and regulatory notification required.

records.title: Field report — Former Employee — ex-Meridian Star Capital fund administrator — SPV structure, Dubai Free Zone
records.text:
A. REPORT. Former Employee — ex-Meridian Star Capital fund administrator describes a network of three SPVs incorporated in Dubai Free Zone between Q3 2022 and Q1 2024, each with a single purpose: to hold a participation interest in a specific cargo trade executed by NEH Dubai Commodities DMCC. The source states that the SPV participations were never disclosed in NEXUS ENERGY HOLDINGS (Cayman)'s consolidated accounts, despite the parent company providing the credit support for all three. The source believes the SPVs were structured specifically to avoid consolidation under IFRS 10 (control-based consolidation standard).

B. SIGNIFICANCE. If the source's account is accurate, this is an off-balance-sheet structuring scheme of the type Enron used via its Raptor SPEs. Under IFRS 10, an entity controls an SPV if it has power over the investee, exposure to variable returns, and the ability to use that power — providing credit support almost certainly establishes all three. Non-consolidation in those circumstances would constitute a material misstatement.

C. COLLECTION NOTE. Location: Dubai Free Zone. Duration: 61 minutes. Documentary evidence described but not yet provided. Source reliability: C. Credibility: 3 (possibly true pending documentation).

records.title: TMS Alert — FICTITIOUS_RECEIVABLE — GOLDEN EAGLE FUND LP (BVI) payment processor, Nicosia Corporate Registry
records.text:
1. SITUATION. The internal audit function, cross-referencing accounts receivable against cash collection records, identified 16 receivable balances totalling $117.1M attributed to a Nicosia Corporate Registry-registered payment processor ('PSP ALPHA NIC') that has no corporate registry entry, no website, and no independently verifiable business activity. KPMG's 2020 special audit could not verify the existence of the cash because it did not exist. The 180+ day non-collection on phantom receivables is precisely the pattern that should have triggered escalation in the Wirecard case.

3. ASSESSMENT. KRI-01 threshold met. Evaluation: A1 — FLASH. Recommend: (a) immediate write-down provisioning; (b) engagement of forensic accountants; (c) notification to auditors; (d) assessment of disclosure obligations under MAR Article 17.

3. ASSESSMENT. KRI-02 (sanctions evasion) and KRI-05 (commodity misreporting) thresholds met simultaneously. Evaluation: A1 — IMMEDIATE. Document hold and regulatory notification required.

This is structurally identical to the Wirecard fraud: €1.9B was booked as escrow receivables from 'third-party acquirers' in Asia (primarily the Senjo Group), none of which had verifiable independent existence. KPMG's 2020 special audit could not verify the existence of the cash because it did not exist. The 180+ day non-collection on phantom receivables is precisely the pattern that should have triggered escalation in the Wirecard case.

3. ASSESSMENT. KRI-01 threshold met. Evaluation: A1 — FLASH. Recommend: (a) immediate write-down provisioning; (b) engagement of forensic accountants; (c) notification to auditors; (d) assessment of disclosure obligations under MAR Article 17.
